threshold_rule: Predict the positive class (attack) when the anomaly score is strictly greater than the threshold. The threshold is the (1 - target_fpr) quantile of benign training anomaly scores (target_fpr=0.01).
training_method: Isolation Forest trained on benign CICIDS2017 flows only. Labels are used only to select those training rows and to build evaluation ground truth. Labels are not model input features.
evaluation_method: Held-out benign flows and attack flows excluded from training. ROC-AUC uses continuous anomaly scores. Accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score use the existing threshold rule, with attack as the positive class.
limitations: Offline CICIDS2017 metrics do not prove real-world zero-day detection performance. An anomaly means unusual behavior versus benign training flows, not confirmation of an attack. The threshold is set from benign training scores, so precision and accuracy depend on the evaluation mix. Attacks that resemble normal traffic can be missed, and rare legitimate traffic can be flagged.
